To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ability of a network to perform learning and memory tasks is constrained by the number of layers, the number of parallel connections, and the number of neurons in a layer.

(1) the ability of an artificial neural network to learn and to remember is influenced by the network's architecture; (2) the ability to learn is enhanced when the number of layers in the network increases; (3) the ability to remember is enhanced when the network is sparser; and (4) a balance between these two abilities can be achieved when the number of hidden units in the network increases.
